newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia cenbank relaxes investment rules further.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia cenbank relaxes investment rules further.

text.p: The Bank of Slovenia said on Tuesday it would allow foreign investors to trade among themselves without incurring extra heavy charges.

The central bank began softening its stance on foreign investment last week with a ruling that funds paid into fiduciary accounts for a seven-year purchase should not be considered a foreign liability.
Banks must balance such liabilities against foreign assets, leading to high charges on the accounts.
The central bank's latest move also exempts trade among foreign investors.
"Balancing will not be necessary when international investors trade among themselves," said Janko Tratnik, head of the central bank's foreign business department.
Banks welcomed the decision, which they said would enable them to reduce the costs of fiduciary accounts significantly.
Banks had estimated the cost of the accounts at roughly 12 percent of the amount handled when balancing was necessary.

"The new decree means that foreigners will be able to trade freely except in cases when they want to sell shares to domestic investors," an analyst said, adding he expected Slovenian stocks to jump on the news.

International investors stopped buying Slovenian securities in February when the central bank decreed they must open fiduciary accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade. Since then the SBI index has dropped by 20 percent.
